lessons.title: Reuniões
lessons.tip: Em inglês de trabalho, «to follow up» e «action item» aparecem em quase todas as atas.

items.example: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow.
Let's stick to the agenda.
Can we reschedule to Thursday?
What was the outcome of the meeting?
Let's wrap up in five minutes.
Each action item needs an owner.

lessons.title: Phrasal verbs do dia a dia
lessons.tip: O sentido de um phrasal verb raramente é a soma das partes. Decora-o como uma palavra nova.

items.example: I can't figure out this bug.
Stop putting off the dentist.
We ran out of coffee.
I'll look into it.
She came up with a great plan.
They get along really well.

lessons.title: Expressões idiomáticas
lessons.tip: Expressões como estas tornam o teu inglês mais natural, mas usa-as com moderação em contexto formal.

items.example: The exam was a piece of cake.
A joke helps to break the ice.
Let's make sure we're on the same page.
It's 7pm, let's call it a day.

items.term: the ball is in your court
items.example: I've sent the offer, the ball is in your court.

items.translation: fazer as coisas à pressa (e mal)
items.example: Don't cut corners on testing.

lessons.title: Falsos amigos
lessons.tip: Estas palavras parecem portuguesas mas significam outra coisa. São das gafes mais comuns.

items.example: Actually, I disagree.
Eventually, he found a job.
He pretended to be asleep.
Push the door, don't pull it.
I borrowed it from the library.
That's a sensible decision.

lessons.title: Emails
lessons.tip: Num email profissional, frases curtas e verbos diretos soam mais seguros do que rodeios.

items.example: Please find attached the report.
As per our call, here are the details.
Looping in Ana from finance.
Just a heads-up: the server goes down at 6.
Please reply at your earliest convenience.
Let's touch base next week.
